newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Ericsson Q1 profits boosted 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ericsson Q1 profits boosted 30 pct.

text.p: Swedish telecommunications giant Ericsson on Friday reported a rise in first quarter profits after financial items to 2.02 billion crowns ($262.9 million), slightly higher than the market expected.
The booming market for mobile phones helped the company and it said it took market share from its competitors.

"Even measured in the increasingly stronger U.S. dollar, order bookings and net sales increased sharply during the first quarter, by 19 percent and 21 percent respectively," chief executive officer Lars Ramqvist said in a statement of results.
The group also said that its mobile systems first quarter order bookings rose 22 percent and that its mobile phones and terminals sales rose almost 100 percent.

"Mobile handsets increased sales by 100 percent in the first quarter but the market hasn't grown that much, consequently we have taken market share," spokesman Per Bengtsson told a telephone conference.
The group said sales in the mobile systems business rose to 12.90 billion crowns from 10.64 billion crowns.
In infocom systems sales were up to 9.28 billion crowns from 7.41 billion crowns and sales in mobile phones and terminals sales rose to 7.62 billion crowns from 3.83 billion crowns.
"Subscriber growth, particularly for digital systems, is very rapid throughout the world," the company said, speaking of the first quarter performance of the mobile systems business.
Net sales in infocom systems rose 19 percent for comparable units but the group said this area faced price pressures.
"As a whole, the result of the business area was weak, due partly to price pressures in the business area's major product areas and continued heavy investments in technical developments," it said.
It said it may be able to improve profitability in the infocoms business due to continued volume growth and realignments of production.
It said the mobile systems and terminals business posted an increase in sales of almost 100 percent.
Analysts said the 30 percent rise in pre-tax profit was a relief for the market after disappointments from drug majors Astra and Pharmacia & Upjohn this week.
"As for the minuses, I would point to the company's negative cashflow and somewhat weaker sales of mobile systems," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
Ericsson dipped in late trading, falling 2.5 crowns to 250.5 crowns in heavy trading of over one billion crowns.
"We think the profit was good, well up to expectations but it is the foreigners who are selling now and pushing the price down," said one Stockholm broker.
